title: Show-business orientation and the dummy playing fourth trombone
summary: Herman encouraged stage antics given his show background, as with Harris's dummy playing fourth trombone at Casino Gardens.

story.theme_name: Band pranks, jokes and gigs gone wrong
story.community_name: Pranks, practical jokes and band humor

blocks.x: Well, I know that -- like, now the Superman act and some of the things that Chubby had done, they were more visual, and early on, was that part of that period, too, that you think, in the '40s and '50s, that the kinds of places you went to to play versus, say, campuses more so, now, that general public might expect a little more of that kind of entertainment?

Well, I don't know, but, you see, that was part of my personal orientation. I came out of show biz and I couldn't see working in a theatre or anyplace where you had a large audience and particularly a mixed audience, all age groupings and so on, where I didn't feel we had to do more than just play some charts.
And I guess I encouraged it among the guys, and very often we had to stow ourselves down because we'd get carried away. We were having so much fun.
Involved in all this and everything that

went on. As soon as I would find out, I would utilize it. Like, Bill Harris and Red Norvell borrowed a couple of lifesized dummies from some girl dancers that worked with these dummies. And they had them dressed in band uniforms.

And Bill was more drastic in his humor than Red, I think, and Bill would keep his dummy in the car with him. Whoever drove with him would have to drive three in the front seat, with the dummy in the middle, and we reached the high point when we opened Tommy Dorsey's place on the beach in Santa Monica, the Casino Gardens. And all of a sudden, I realized that we had four trombones, and the dummy was playing fourth trombone.

And then all night Bill was arguing with him. Every time there was a two-part bars out, he was having a terrible beef with this dummy. It just held the trombone all night. He said, 'Man, come in when I tell you.'
